evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv rows 1880–1881; pipeline/data/unihan-kmandarin-hsk1.tsv row 302; sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt rows 29904–29912 and 146271–146286
evidence.text: The local Baxter–Sagart rows give 丂: Mandarin kǎo, Middle Chinese khawX, Old Chinese *C.qʰˤuʔ, gloss “to sob,” and 考: Mandarin kǎo, Middle Chinese khawX, Old Chinese *k-r̥ˤuʔ, gloss “old; deceased father.” These are Baxter–Sagart system 1.1 readings; the distinct Old Chinese forms do not show an identical reconstructed pronunciation. The local Unihan rows give current kMandarin kǎo for both characters. U+8003’s official Unihan URL could not be opened, so these local rows are not presented as externally verified Unihan evidence.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup (record URL attempted; inaccessible)

evidence.text: The database reports competing accounts for 丂: one identifies its early form as a branch or forked branch (with a previous proposal of an axe handle); another proposes that 考 depicts an old person holding a staff, with 丂 as both semantic and phonetic. It reports early 丂 uses as a place name on oracle bones and sound loans for 考 meaning father and 孝 in bronze inscriptions. It also cites the Shuowen account of 丂 as obstructed breath. These are source-reported analyses, not direct image inspection in this research.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：丂

evidence.field: 考: form and meaning account, lines 169–179
evidence.text: The database presents a distinction between early Western Zhou bronze use of 老 for both “old” and “father,” and a later differentiated 考 graph; it attributes the analysis of 考 as 老 plus phonetic 丂 to Xu Shen. It separately gives an alternative account deriving 考 as a differentiating graph from an already borrowed 丂 meaning “father.” Bronze inscriptions use 考 for father and also attest it borrowed for assessing/considering and for 孝; the site cites the Zhongshan Wang Ding and excavated Chu bamboo texts. It cautions that 考 in father terms is often deceased father but not exclusively so. This evidence does not establish a simple chronological semantic chain from father to examine.
evidence.title: 考 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, seal, clerical and regular-script forms, including bronze examples assigned to Western Zhou through Warring States and a Qin slip record. Its prose adopts the 老省 plus 丂 phonetic account and says later clerical forms significantly altered the older shape. It also repeats a 老/考 轉注 interpretation. The narrative is one account and conflicts with the alternative oracle-form analysis; glyph images were not visually inspected.
evidence.title: 考字形演变字源

evidence.field: 考, 老部; Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: Shuowen records “老也。从老省，丂聲” (old; from abbreviated 老, 丂 phonetic). Duan Yucai distinguishes the base sense of longevity, extension to “completion,” and borrowing for 攷 in senses such as strike, examine, or question. This is a historical lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of the graph’s original formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「考」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: 攷 is defined with the Shuowen analysis “叩也。从攴，丂聲” (knock; from 攴, 丂 phonetic), with senses striking and checking/examining, and is listed as a variant of 考. The source preserves both the older graphic distinction in the Shuowen entry and later overlap with 考; it does not establish when the forms became interchangeable.
evidence.title: B01464 攷 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 攷 and 考 sense comparison, lines 31–38
evidence.text: The comparison lists 攷 as striking and examining, later written 考, and also as used for 考 meaning deceased father; it lists 考 senses including old/longevity, completion, deceased father, examination, questioning and investigation. The list is not dated and cannot by itself establish a chronology of semantic development.
evidence.title: 異體字「攷」與「考」的字義比較

evidence.source: Japanese Wiktionary, citing 季旭昇 and 李春桃
evidence.field: 考 etymology and cited bibliography, lines 139–156
evidence.text: This account calls 考 a differentiated form of 老 used by phonetic loan for the Chinese word meaning “think/consider,” and explicitly rejects the Shuowen component analysis based on oracle forms. It cites 季旭昇《說文新証》 (2014, pp. 668–670) and 李春桃’s 2020 study on 丂. The word’s pronunciation and the graph’s graphic origin are presented as separate questions here.
evidence.title: 考 — ウィクショナリー日本語版

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction, version 1.1 data table
evidence.field: Local TSV entries cross-checked against published reconstruction table
evidence.text: Baxter–Sagart’s reconstructed 考 *k-r̥ˤuʔ is not the same as the local 丂 *C.qʰˤuʔ entry, while both have Middle Chinese khawX in the local table. Therefore shared current Mandarin kǎo and identical Middle Chinese transcriptions do not on their own verify 丂 as a phonetic in 考 under this reconstruction. Another system may yield a closer relationship; reconstructions must not be merged across systems.
evidence.title: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

gaps: The direct official Unicode per-character record URLs for 考 U+8003 and 丂 U+4E02 were attempted but inaccessible. Local current kMandarin rows were checked for both; external verification of the exact records remains unavailable.

No primary oracle-bone or bronze glyph image was visually inspected. Reported glyph shapes and datings are secondary database descriptions; fine-grained graphic change and any graphic corruption cannot be asserted from this research.

The sound history is unresolved: local Baxter–Sagart readings do not align as identical Old Chinese forms, and no opened primary source supplied paired reconstructions for 丂 and 考 within another system. A phonetic role is asserted in traditional and modern accounts but remains disputed.

A cited CUHK entry reports oracle-bone 丂 chiefly as a place name and bronze loans as 考 (father) and 孝; it does not establish the original spoken name of the proposed branch/staff object. Thus the object-name-based sound explanation is unverified.

Earliest graph attestation and earliest attested lexical sense are not fully settled. Available pages list Shang oracle forms and Western Zhou bronze cases but give no independently checked dated inscription reading for the exact earliest use.

Although bronze and Warring States examples support both father-related and assessing/examining usages, the semantic link from old/longevity or father to examine/test is not demonstrated; do not present the senses as a proven chronological chain.
No license or reuse terms for the recurrent CUHK database material were verified; recommend citation and paraphrase only, not a local extract.
攷 is defined separately in Shuowen as “叩也” with 攴 plus 丂, while later references classify it as a variant of 考. The timing and extent of this graphic and semantic overlap remain unclear.
